description:
Fetch the current screen of a running React Native app as a compact tree of React components.
Each on-screen component is listed with its name, its text (or accessibilityLabel when it has no
text), [testID=…] and normalized (tap: x,y) centre in [0,1] (fractions of the screen, not pixels).
Full-screen transparent wrappers and implementation-detail components are pruned. Wrappers the size
of their parent are pruned too, so a missing name proves nothing: check with debugger-inspect-element.

Use when you need what describe does not show: a testID for a selector (on Android, describe omits
the testID of a view that has no label and is not tappable), or the component names and nesting
behind the screen before editing code. To find what to tap, use describe.

On an iOS simulator with a landscape UI (a rotated device, or an unfolded foldable), the tap
coordinates are on the screen's axes, which the gesture tools use.
Returns a compact text tree; call again after navigation. Fails if the Metro debugger is not connected.

device_id.description: Device id from list-devices: the SAME id you passed to debugger-connect (iOS simulator UDID or Android serial).

includeSkipped.description: When true, appends a summary of all filtered components: total fiber count and skip counts by component name and by filter. Default: false.

maxNodes.description: Maximum total nodes to include. When exceeded, intermediate single-child wrapper chains are collapsed to preserve both root structure and leaf elements. Default: no limit.

onScreenOnly.description: When true, only components visible on screen are returned. Set to false to include all mounted components, including those scrolled off-screen, e.g. to understand the full page structure. Default: true.

port.description: Metro port. Omit it to use this device's port (8081 by default). Ignored for Chromium, whose CDP port is in device_id. Range: 1 to 65535.

udid.description: iOS simulator UDID from list-devices. Pass it when device_id is a logicalDeviceId (two or more devices share one Metro), so that the tap coordinates of a landscape UI are on the screen's axes. Give the UDID of the simulator that shows the app.

name: debugger-component-tree
